newsitem.title: USA: Dade County, Fla., mulls sale of call waivers.
newsitem.headline: Dade County, Fla., mulls sale of call waivers.

text.p: Florida's Dade County is considering a proposal to sell call waivers on two general obligation bond series totalling $75 million, Finance Manager Rachel Baum said Tuesday.

"This I believe has been successful in the commercial market. It has not been done that much in the tax-exempt market," Baum said after a meeting of the Dade County Budget, Finance and Public Trust Committee. "We believe there's a market for it."
The proposal was put forth by Raymond James & Associates Inc, which is a member of the county's bond underwriting pool.

The county can conservatively expect $4 million from the waiver sale, Raymond James' officials told the committee. The portion of the bonds not tendered under the waiver sale would be refunded, by competitive bid, Baum said.
The issues in question are Dade County Public Improvement Series DD and Series 1988, which were both issued in 1988.
The proposal will go before the full commission on May 20.

The county had considered selling waivers for five issues totalling $198 million, but officials said Tuesday that they believe the bond documents for the remaining three issues required that calls be all-or-none.
Those three GO series, totalling about $123 million, will still be refunded via competitive bid, Baum said.
The county has one other sale pending, a $130 million aviation refunding series scheduled to price next week via Bear Stearns & Co Inc.
